feedback: Wired the toolchain-spike artifacts from iteration 6 (UniFFI-generated native_bridge.kt, cross-compiled libnative_bridge.so for arm64-v8a/x86_64) into the actual Gradle build and MainActivity, closing out devsystem.android_native_bridge's Gradle-integration slice. Added net.java.dev.jna:jna:5.17.0@aar to app/build.gradle.kts -- verified as the only dependency needed by reading native_bridge.kt's imports directly (only com.sun.jna.*), not by guessing; the @aar classifier requirement and minimum version were cross-checked against UniFFI's own Kotlin Gradle guide. Deliberately did NOT add kotlinx-coroutines-core: the generated file's 'Async support' section is an empty comment header, since bridge_version() isn't an async UniFFI export -- adding an unused dependency would have been guessing, not verifying. MainActivity now calls the real uniffi.native_bridge.bridgeVersion() (a genuine JNA FFI call into libnative_bridge.so) and renders its return value, wrapped in a catch(e: LinkageError) fallback. That fallback isn't speculative defensive coding -- the first hermetic test run actually failed with UnsatisfiedLinkError, because libnative_bridge.so is cross-compiled by cargo-ndk against Android's Bionic libc and cannot load under Robolectric's host-JVM/glibc test environment; the fallback and an updated MainActivityTest make that a real, exercised code path instead of a build break. Verified hermetically via mingc/android-build-box (this run's established pattern): ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest assembleDebug --no-daemon --stacktrace -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 1 test / 0 failures. Verified both ABI .so files are actually packaged inside app-debug.apk (not just present on disk) via a zipfile listing: lib/arm64-v8a/libnative_bridge.so and lib/x86_64/libnative_bridge.so, both present with real non-zero sizes. Pushed to CADS-webconference-android@f406927 (aa8696d..f406927). NOT verified and not claimed: real on-device/emulator execution -- this host has no working Android emulator, so nothing here proves the app actually displays the real bridge_version() string when launched. What was verified is that the code builds, both ABI native libs ship inside the APK, and the LinkageError fallback path is real and exercised (proving the FFI call is genuinely wired, not stubbed) -- the success-path render on a real device remains unverified pending real-device access.

proposals.rationale: Discovered while doing this iteration's work, not speculatively: native-bridge/build-android.sh's own header comment states the .so/.kt artifacts it produces 'are committed for now (this is still the toolchain spike, not yet CI-integrated -- see the #382 run notes for the follow-up to build these from source in CI instead)'. Right now app/src/main/jniLibs/*/libnative_bridge.so and app/src/main/java/uniffi/native_bridge/native_bridge.kt are manually generated on a developer/agent host and committed as opaque binary + generated-source artifacts -- CI (devsystem.verify's GitHub Actions run) only ever compiles the Kotlin/Gradle side and never rebuilds them from native-bridge/src/lib.rs. For a toolchain spike with a trivial bridge_version() function this is a low-stakes gap, but it will not remain low-stakes: this same path is slated to carry the real Noise_IK/Agent-Fabric crypto code (per #382's plan), at which point an unreproducible, manually-regenerated .so sitting in git history becomes a real supply-chain and correctness concern (no CI proof the committed binary matches the committed Rust source). Proposing a stage that runs native-bridge/build-android.sh (or an equivalent cargo-ndk + uniffi-bindgen invocation) inside CI and either verifies the committed artifacts are reproducible or replaces committing them at all in favor of a CI-produced build output.
